page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and two threads per core. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, allocating 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware support includes Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512, AVX-VNNI) alongside Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and AMX int8), backed by 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 480 MB L3 cache. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by support for remote Premium Storage. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network and gateway routing. Synthetic tests show steady I/O and transaction capability, recording 2,860.88 operations on PassMark database benchmarks, 8.24 million operations per second during Redis SET workloads, and 8.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, with single-core gzip compression registering 36.47 GB/sec in the top decile and bzip3 decompression achieving 15.05 GB/sec. Tradeoffs appear in multi-threaded density and uncached memory operations; stress-ng multi-core testing (4,653.8) and large block memory writes (23.77 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile due to the two physical core constraint. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of direct NVMe storage and dedicated compute cycles optimizes resource allocation for mid-tier enterprise deployments. Typical fitting workloads include web applications, intermediate caching tiers, containerized microservices, and lightweight database instances requiring local scratch disk performance.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 16.0 GB of memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 and AMX. Dedicated local storage consists of a 236 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU accelerators are bundled. Benchmark data highlights strong single-threaded compression performance at 36.47 GB/sec alongside average database and static web serving metrics, though multi-core throughput and memory write bandwidth reflect the physical core limitations. The combination of dedicated compute cycles, integrated NVMe disk, and balanced memory allocation provides practical resource efficiency for intermediate enterprise workloads, including web servers, distributed caching layers, application backends, and low-concurrency database environments.
